title: Large Schröder numbers: the sharp tripling step 3·L(n) ≤ L(n+1) and the lower bound L(n) ≥ 2·3^(n-1)

problemStatement.plain: The large Schröder numbers count lattice paths from (0,0) to (n,n) using steps East, North, and Diagonal that never go above the main diagonal (equivalently, certain Schröder paths / super-Catalan structures). They satisfy a self-convolution recurrence: the next term is the current term plus the convolution sum of all earlier terms.

two_mul_three_pow_le_largeSchroder_succ (:77): 2·3^n≤L(n+1) all n by tripling-driven induction
insights: Tripling comes from keeping BOTH extreme convolution terms i=0 and i=n (each = L(0)·L(n)=L(n)); parent kept only i=0 → doubling.
Constant 3 is SHARP: equality 3·L(1)=L(2)=6 at n=1. Asymptotic ratio is larger (3+2√2≈5.828); gap = discarded interior terms.
Hypothesis n≥1 necessary: at n=0 indices 0 and n collapse to one term, tripling fails (3·L0=3>2=L1).
nextSteps: Push constant past 3 toward 3+2√2 by bounding interior convolution terms.
Prove dominance L(n)≥catalan(n) by recurrence comparison (Dyck⊂Schröder paths).
